text: OmicSelector R package biomarker discovery enforces methodologically sound machine learning practices. Built mlr3 ecosystem, guarantees: Zero Data Leakage: Feature selection occurs strictly inside cross-validation folds Proper Nested CV: Separation outer (evaluation) inner (selection) loops Feature Stability: Nogueira Stability Index reproducible biomarker sets Multi-Objective Selection: Balance performance, stability, parsimony

what: Hurdle Filter for Zero-Inflated Data — FilterHurdle
title: Hurdle Filter for Zero-Inflated Data — FilterHurdle
text: Two-part filter designed zero-inflated count/expression data. Tests difference zero-frequency difference magnitude among non-zero values.

title: Hurdle Filter for Zero-Inflated Data — FilterHurdle
text: Hurdle filter combines two tests: 1. **Binary component**: Chi-square test zero vs non-zero contingency table 2. **Continuous component**: Wilcoxon test non-zero values score computed using Fisher's method combine p-values: chi2 = -2 * sum(log(p_values)) captures genes good biomarkers : - detectable one class (zero-frequency difference) - upregulated one class among expressed samples (magnitude difference)

text: OmicSelector 2.4.0 toolkit high-dimensional biomarker discovery leakage-resistant validation, stable feature selection, within-sample panel methods, frozen-reference denoising add-ons, qPCR non-detect handling, matched-null benchmarks, provenance-aware audit helpers.

title: OmicSelector: Zero-Leakage Biomarker Discovery Toolkit — OmicSelector-package
text: ## Key Features - **Zero Data Leakage**: preprocessing, feature selection, model training   occurs within proper cross-validation folds via mlr3 GraphLearners. - **Nested Cross-Validation**: Inner loop feature selection hyperparameter   tuning, outer loop unbiased performance estimation. - **Stability Metrics**: Nogueira Stability Index ensure selected features   robust across resamples, just high accuracy. - **Reproducibility**: renv lockfiles, Docker containers, deterministic pipelines. - **Panel Governance**: Group-aware resampling, provenance-floor diagnostics,   identifiability gates, matched-null benchmarks, operating-point summaries   biomarker panels evaluated public omics data. ## Core Classes - [OmicPipeline]: Central R6 class creating leakage-free pipelines - [BenchmarkService]: Enforces proper nested cross-validation ## Quick Start “`r library(OmicSelector) # Create pipeline data pipeline <- OmicPipeline$new(   data = my_data,   target = "outcome",   positive = "Case" ) # Create graph learner feature selection learner <- pipeline$create_graph_learner(   filter = "anova",   model = "ranger",   n_features = 20 ) # Run nested CV benchmark service <- BenchmarkService$new(pipeline, outer_folds = 5, inner_folds = 3) service$add_learner(learner) result <- service$run() “` ## Philosophy OmicSelector 2.4.0 prioritizes leakage-resistant validation, feature stability, auditable provenance checks raw apparent accuracy. High accuracy unstable feature sets strong provenance-prediction treated warning signal rather direct biomarker evidence.

title: Hybrid Sequential Feature Selection (HSFS) — SequentialSelector
text: Implements multi-stage feature reduction pipeline handle high-dimensional omics data efficiently. pipeline chains: 1. Variance thresholding (remove near-zero variance) 2. Univariate filtering (ANOVA F-test) 3. RF importance filtering (single-pass, iterative RFE) 4. AUC filter final selection (univariate ranking AUC) Note: RF importance stage single-pass approximation using Random Forest variable importance, true iterative Recursive Feature Elimination. final stage uses univariate AUC filtering (LASSO regularization). hybrid approach outperforms single-method selection high-dimensional data.

what: CoDA-Aware Feature Selection for Biomarker Panels — coda-feature-selection
title: CoDA-Aware Feature Selection for Biomarker Panels — coda-feature-selection
text: Feature-selection methods tailored compositional omics data. exported functions return per-feature importance scores selected features, accompanying `mlr3filters::Filter` classes expose methods inside existing `OmicPipeline` feature-selection path. implemented selectors cover five complementary CoDA-aware strategies: - `codaFS_plr_variance()`: pairwise log-ratio screening feature   aggregation. - `codaFS_selbal_wrapper()`: sparse forward-balance selection using   official `selbal` package available, native fallback. - `codaFS_codacore_wrapper()`: sparse balance selection via CoDaCoRe using   existing OmicSelector interface. - `codaFS_logcontrast_lasso()`: CLR-space lasso post-fit zero-sum   projection. - `codaFS_stability_logratio()`: stability selection pairwise log-ratio   features elastic-net aggregation back individual miRNAs.

title: Decompose Brier Score — decompose_brier
text: Brier score decomposes : $$Brier = Reliability - Resolution + Uncertainty$$ - **Reliability** (calibration): measures deviation perfect calibration - **Resolution**: measures much predictions differ across groups - **Uncertainty**: base rate positive class, p(1-p) well-calibrated model low reliability high resolution.

Per-feature variance truly load-bearing (scalar heuristic).

title: Frozen ComBat for Leakage-Free Batch Correction — frozen-combat
text: Implements "frozen" version ComBat batch correction prevents data leakage external validation. Standard ComBat estimates batch parameters data, causes leakage applied train+test together. Frozen ComBat separates parameter estimation (training ) application (data).

title: Frozen ComBat for Leakage-Free Batch Correction — frozen-combat
text: ## Frozen ComBat? Standard ComBat workflow: “` combined_data <- rbind(train, test) corrected <- ComBat(combined_data, batch)  # LEAKAGE: test data influences correction “` Frozen ComBat workflow: “` frozen <- FrozenComBat$new() frozen$fit(train_data, train_batch)         # Learn parameters training corrected_train <- frozen$transform(train_data, train_batch) corrected_test <- frozen$transform(test_data, test_batch)  # Apply frozen parameters “`

title: Model Interpretability for OmicSelector — interpretability
text: ## Interpretability Matters biomarker discovery, understanding model makes predictions important accuracy. Key use cases: - Identify genes/miRNAs drive classification - Detect potential confounders batch effects - Generate hypotheses biological validation - Build trust clinical adoption ## Methods Provided - **Feature Importance**: Permutation-based importance (model-agnostic) - **Partial Dependence**: features affect predictions marginally - **SHAP Values**: Additive feature attributions (via iml approximation) - **Correlation Warnings**: Flag high-correlation features may mislead ## Fold-Aware Design interpretability methods respect cross-validation structure: - Explanations computed per-fold using training data - Aggregated explanations show stability across folds - Unstable features flagged

"fixed": pseudocount across features, given         value (default 1.0). Backward-compatible         log2(x + 1) convention. title: Paper 3 within-sample compositional methods (Module A, P1) — paper3-within-sample
text: Five Module-within-sample compositional transforms introduced Paper 3 OmicSelector programme (Stawiski et al., preparation; Nature Methods target). methods single-sample reference-cohort-free: sample normalised, scored, projected using panel values, requirement external training cohort exist deployment time. property makes within-sample methods suitable clinical translation: diagnostic test built primitives can deployed computing per-patient score patient's panel measurement, without re-fitting normalization population reference. Methods provided: ws_rclr_trimmed: robust trimmed centred log-ratio     optional zero-detection-convention; tolerant dominant     contaminating species (haemolysis miRNAs) small-head--pool     compositions typical plasma/serum miRNA panels. ws_balance_ilr: orthonormal isometric log-ratio     balances frozen sequential binary partition encoding circulating     miRNA biology (red-blood-cell vs rest, platelet vs rest, let-7 family     within-cluster, miR-17~92, miR-200, miR-371~373, dominant-vs-tail     abundance balance). ws_alr_pivot: additive log-ratio frozen     pivot pool putatively low-variance circulating miRNAs serving     geometric-mean denominator (anchors transformation     stable internal reference rather choosing single feature     denominator). ws_mad_logratio: median-centred log-ratio     optional per-sample MAD scaling; Aitchison-valid robust     descriptive transform downstream learners require     zero-sum compositional coordinates. ws_dominance_score: panel-internal scalar QC     dominance score reporting fraction total panel signal carried     top-K features; flags pre-analytical failures (haemolysis,     incomplete extraction) calibrated Tier R reference     distribution. Helper utilities provided alongside: ws_default_sbp returns curated v1 sequential-binary-partition tree circulating miRNA panels, ws_default_pivot_pool returns curated v1 ALR pivot pool (six low-variance miRNAs; miR-92a-3p excluded recent serum/plasma literature treats erythrocyte-derived).

title: Paper 3 within-sample compositional methods (Module A, P1) — paper3-within-sample
text: Background: circulating miRNA biomarkers proposed minimally invasive cancer markers 2008 (Mitchell et al., PNAS). intervening years clinically actionable cancer-screening test emerged source despite thousands "candidate panel" papers. reasons predominantly technical (batch effects, hemolysis contamination, lack standards, reference-cohort dependency, cross-cohort leakage, absence provenance/claim-gating) rather biological. five within-sample compositional methods target two failure modes directly: reference-cohort dependency (method scores single sample using panel values) contamination dominant erythrocyte-derived species (miR-451a, miR-486-5p, miR-16, miR-144-3p, miR-92a-3p - explicitly handled either exclusion rCLR centering subset dedicated balances SBP tree). Module one six modules OmicSelector v2.4 toolkit. modules - Module B (hemolysis correction), Module C (frozen batch correction), Module D (outlier detection conformal claim-gating), Module E (multi-cancer / domain generalisation), Module F (self-supervised pretraining ablation) - documented Paper 3 Methods per-module help pages.

what: Block-aware two-stage BH-FDR for specimen-shared cohort clusters — paper3_bh_fdr_correct_blocked
title: Block-aware two-stage BH-FDR for specimen-shared cohort clusters — paper3_bh_fdr_correct_blocked
text: Naïve BH-FDR within modality family treats specimen-shared cohorts (e.g., Toray clusters \(\sim 94.5\%\) specimen reuse) independent tests, anti-conservative due strongly correlated test statistics. function implements two-stage correction: Within provenance block, combine cohort-level p-values via     Fisher's chi-square statistic. Two reference distributions     reported side side: conservative reference: \(S/c\)         \(\chi^2_{2k}\); intentionally conservative; used         manuscript's headline counts. textbook reference (Brown 1975 / Kost-McDermott 2002):         \(S/c\) \(\chi^2_{2k/c}\) \(df\) rescaled         inflation factor. Apply BH-FDR across block-level p-values, separately     reference. inflation factor \(c(k) = 1 + (k - 1)\rho\) \(k\) number cohorts block \(\rho\) assumed within-block correlation (default \(\rho = 0.25\) reproduces manuscript's headline).

what: Nogueira Stability Index for Feature Selection — stability
title: Nogueira Stability Index for Feature Selection — stability
text: Functions computing Nogueira Stability Index, measures consistency feature selection across cross-validation folds.

title: Nogueira Stability Index for Feature Selection — stability
text: Nogueira Stability Index preferred Jaccard/Kuncheva indices invariant number selected features. high stability (close 1) indicates features consistently selected across different training subsets, suggesting robust signal rather overfitting specific data splits. Formula: $$S = 1 - \frac{V}{V_0}$$ : - V = (1/p) * sum(pi_j * (1 - pi_j)) [observed variance] - V_0 = (k_bar/p) * (1 - k_bar/p) [expected variance random selection] - pi_j = selection frequency feature j - k_bar = average number selected features - p = total number candidate features

what: Within-Sample Normalization for Biomarker Panels — within-sample
title: Within-Sample Normalization for Biomarker Panels — within-sample
text: Functions within-sample normalization operate single sample's feature values. methods use population-level statistics — sample normalized independently using feature values — cancel specific classes per-sample nuisance variation WITHOUT reference cohort. Invariance scope method-specific (see Details). methods general "batch-effect remover": gene-specific batch effects, non-linear platform response, measurement-specific bias cancelled. key insight clinical deployment: diagnostic test based within-sample normalization requires reference cohort. Draw blood, measure k biomarkers, compute relative pattern, classify.

title: Within-Sample Normalization for Biomarker Panels — within-sample
text: Within-sample normalization addresses one component batch-effect problem circulating biomarker diagnostics: per-sample nuisance variation (collection-site offset, loading amount, total-library scaling). Traditional normalization methods (quantile, ComBat, z-score) require reference population, impractical point--care diagnostics. Within-sample methods sidestep reference-cohort requirement specific, narrower invariance scope: ws_logratio / ws_ratio_image: additive-shift-invariant     log-space (equivalently, invariant multiplicative per-sample     factor applied UNIFORMLY across features raw space).     invariant gene-specific shifts non-linear platform response. ws_zscore: invariant affine per-sample transforms     (scale + shift) applied uniformly across features. ws_rank: invariant strictly monotonic per-sample     transform features. ws_minmax: invariant uniform per-sample affine transforms     sensitive outlier features. Available methods: ws_minmax: Scale sample's features [0,1] ws_rank: Replace values within-sample ranks ws_zscore: Standardize across features within sample ws_logratio: Compute pairwise log-ratios (self-normalizing) ws_ratio_image: Create pairwise ratio matrix (CNN input)

title: Additive log-ratio with a frozen pivot pool — ws_alr_pivot
text: Within-sample additive log-ratio (ALR) transformation using frozen pivot pool housekeeping-like miRNAs geometric-mean denominator. $$x_{\mathrm{alr},} = \log(x_i + c) - \log(\mathrm{gmean}(x_{\mathrm{pivot}} + c))$$ Anchors transformation stable internal reference rather choosing single feature denominator (classical Aitchison ALR). Fail-closed default: refuses compute fewer min_pivot_present pivots present input panel, unless operator explicitly opts global rCLR fallback. Silent substitution -feature centering curated denominator can mask haemolysis platelet contamination - flagged codex Round 1 review.

title: Isometric log-ratio balances on a frozen partition tree — ws_balance_ilr
text: Computes orthonormal isometric log-ratio (ILR) balances frozen sequential binary partition. partition (G+, G-) balance $$b = \sqrt{\frac{|G+|\,|G-|}{|G+| + |G-|}} \log\!\left(\frac{\mathrm{gmean}(x_{G+})}{\mathrm{gmean}(x_{G-})}\right).$$ default partition (ws_default_sbp) encodes circulating miRNA biology: erythrocyte-vs-rest, platelet-vs-rest, let-7 family within-cluster, miR-17~92, miR-200, miR-371~373, dominant-vs-tail abundance balance computed runtime. title: OmicSelector 2.4.0 (2026-05-07)
text: Round 3 additions (2026-05-07) — manuscript-alignment patches (Paper 3 audit patches 1 9; orchestrator patch 10 deferred): Added qPCR non-detect handling R/paper3-nondetects.R: qpcr_nondetect_impute() (Bayesian hierarchical imputation via nondetects Bioconductor package, fall-LOD nondetects, HTqPCR, Biobase unavailable) qpcr_nondetect_lod_fallback() (limit--detection fallback Ct = 40). Mirrors manuscript Methods §“Non-detect handling quantitative PCR data”. Added nondetects, HTqPCR, Biobase Suggests:. Added hemolysis_index_blondal() R/paper3-hemolysis.R: Blondal-style log(miR-451a) − log(miR-23a-3p) helper accepting canonical mature miRNA names MIMAT accessions. Closes manuscript-claimed Blondal-canonical hemolysis index gap; pair fit_hemolysis_rr() / apply_hemolysis_rr() manuscript-specified Module B nuisance correction. Added os_provenance_preflight() R/paper3-provenance-preflight.R: specimen-overlap pre-flight gate reads TSV manifest returns one NO_OVERLAP, KNOWN_OVERLAP, UNKNOWN_ACCESSION. Ships curated default manifest inst/extdata/provenance_manifest.tsv covering Toray-3D cluster, Toray-V20 cluster, COSMOS-LDCT pair, VUMC-PDAC NanoString pair, audited-independent accessions used manuscript. Added paper3_matched_null_benchmark_cv() R/paper3-matched-null.R: 5-fold nested-CV matched-null benchmark (panel selection univariate AUC training fold; matched-null strata computed training fold; held-test fold scored). Supports grouped folds via group_id, deterministic per-draw seeding via v0.6_per_draw_seed_schedule_independent RNG protocol, three-tier matched-null fallback. engine produced manuscript’s per-cell numbers; promoting OmicSelector_paper/code/methods/matched_null_benchmark.R makes headline tables figures reproducible package alone. Extended paper3_bh_fdr_correct_blocked(): now reports conservative reference (q_block_BH, p_block; S/c chi-square(2k)) textbook Brown 1975 / Kost-McDermott 2002 reference (q_block_BH_textbook, p_block_textbook; S/c chi-square(2k/c)). Added rho argument (default 0.25) manuscript-required sensitivity analysis rho ∈ {0.10, 0.50, 1.00} can reproduced package. Backwards-compatible: existing call signatures continue work rho default reproduces previous numerical behaviour exactly. New columns added, replaced. Added auc_ci_method argument paper3_matched_null_benchmark() paper3_matched_null_benchmark_cv(): "hanley_mcneil" (default; closed-form Hanley-McNeil 1982 SE), "delong" (via pROC::ci.auc(method = "delong"); pooled fold-level scores CV variant), "none". Returns auc_obs_ci_lo / auc_obs_ci_hi alongside auc_obs / auc_obs_cv. Closes v5 per-cell-AUC-CI gap flagged manuscript Discussion. Exported paper3_hanley_mcneil_auc_ci() user-facing Hanley-McNeil 1982 AUC confidence-interval helper used internally matched-null benchmark functions. Added min_balance_coverage argument ws_balance_ilr() (default 0.8, per manuscript Methods §“Within-sample compositional methods”). input panel computes fewer 80% eight balances, returned vector / matrix filled NA carries attr(., "coverage_failed") <- TRUE attr(., "coverage") let caller distinguish coverage failure real -NA cell. Behaviour change: previously function silently returned partially-NA vector. Existing callers need old behaviour can pass min_balance_coverage = 0. Documented ws_alr_pivot() fail-closed default roxygen @details. Default remains allow_global_fallback = FALSE; manuscript pipeline opts via allow_global_fallback = TRUE per-cell logging. code change beyond docstring. Bumped DESCRIPTION version 2.3.0.9000 2.4.0. Release-check notes: R CMD check ---cran may report CRAN incoming NOTEs new submission, tarball size, optional catboost / selbal backends mainstream CRAN/Bioconductor repositories. optional backend/release-distribution notes, package-code warnings. Added unit tests every new entry point: tests/testthat/ test-paper3-nondetects.R, test-paper3-provenance-preflight.R, test-paper3-hemolysis.R (Blondal index block), test-paper3-matched-null.R (rho / textbook / per-cell AUC CI / nested-CV blocks), test-paper3-within-sample.R (ILR coverage block). Patch 10 (end--end pipeline orchestrator wrapping OmicSelector_paper/code/run_paper3_pipeline.R omicselector_paper3_run()) deferred follow-release; manuscript-alignment gap remains round.
